summary.text: A 42-year-old Malay man, a dental technologist and active smoker with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus and dyslipidaemia, was diagnosed with multifocal lacunar infarctions in 2022. A first episode of left-sided weakness improved within 24 hours and a week later a second episode brought slurred speech, hemiplegic gait, facial asymmetry and left-sided hemiparesis.

Computed tomography at the hospital showed recent infarctions in the right anterior temporal lobe, corona radiata, basal ganglia and occipital lobe. He was treated for young stroke and his motor function improved over a month. He returned to work early, made errors with denture orders, was reprimanded and sought treatment for low mood.

A family medicine specialist found normal vital signs, neurological findings and blood tests, motor strength 5/5 and independence in daily activities, while the post-stroke checklist showed cognitive and work difficulty. The MoCA score was 24, indicating mild cognitive impairment, and PHQ-9 and Two Questions with Help Question scores were normal, with no feature suggesting depression or post-stroke dementia. Medications were optimised and an interdisciplinary team planned rehabilitation, workplace modification and monitoring.

The patient responded favourably to the rehabilitation goals and light-duty measures and gradually recovered from the psychological impact of the work-related incident. His MoCA score improved to 30/30 within 6 weeks of intervention, and consequently he successfully returned to his work.

article_limitations: The source has no figures, no supplementary material and no media; raw.xml contains no supplementary-material element.

Almost no event has a calendar date; only the stroke month (April 2022), the first-week interval to the second episode and the 6-week MoCA interval are timed, so most events are ordered only where the text states order.
The post-stroke checklist rows, Table 2 and the MoCA domain Table 3 are stated without per-item dates; Table 3 is general background.
The refused referral is a counsellor or psychiatrist in the text and a counsellor or psychologist in Table 2; both are review-only.
The post-stroke checklist mood item (anxious or depressed) is review-only because it joins two states.
The MoCA paragraph opens with 'Thereafter' after Table 1; as a paragraph-opening order word it is not used to order the MoCA after the specialist assessment.
